lines.text: Main mode steps (Figure 8-4, R1 initiator, R2 responder):
lines.spoken: Main mode steps (Figure 8-4, R 1 initiator, R 2 responder):

lines.text: 1. R1 sends its two configured ISAKMP proposals (the figure shows DES, MD5, DH1 and AES, SHA, DH2, all pre-shared).
lines.spoken: 1. R 1 sends its two configured ice-a-camp proposals (the figure shows D.E.S., M.D. 5, D.H. 1 and A.E.S., SHA, D.H. 2, all pre-shared).

lines.text: 2. R2 finds a match (AES, SHA, DH2, pre-shared) and sends back the accepted proposal.
lines.spoken: 2. R 2 finds a match (A.E.S., SHA, D.H. 2, pre-shared) and sends back the accepted proposal.

lines.text: 3. R1 starts Diffie-Hellman: sends the KE payload and a nonce.
lines.spoken: 3. R 1 starts Diffie Hellman: sends the KE payload and a nonce.

lines.text: 4. R2 sends its KE and nonce and uses the Diffie-Hellman group to generate the SKEYID.
lines.spoken: 4. R 2 sends its KE and nonce and uses the Diffie Hellman group to generate the S key I.D.

lines.text: 5. R1 sends its identity, encrypted with keying from the SKEYID.
lines.spoken: 5. R 1 sends its identity, encrypted with keying from the S key I.D.

lines.text: 6. R2 validates R1 and sends its own identity, also encrypted.
lines.spoken: 6. R 2 validates R 1 and sends its own identity, also encrypted.

lines.text: IKEv2 supports next-generation encryption and anti-DoS.

lines.text: IKEv1 and IKEv2 are incompatible. An IKEv1 device can't build a tunnel with an IKEv2 device.
lines.spoken: IKEv1 and IKEv2 are incompatible. An IKEv1 device can't build a tunnel with an IKEv2 device.

lines.text: DoS risk: key material is exchanged in the first two messages (SA_INIT), so spoofed SA_INIT floods make the gateway spend resources. The stateless cookie fixes this. The book says this attack hits an "IKEv1-enabled device", but SA_INIT is an IKEv2 message, so it means an IKEv2 gateway.
lines.spoken: D.O.S. risk: key material is exchanged in the first two messages (SA_INIT), so spoofed SA_INIT floods make the gateway spend resources. The stateless cookie fixes this. The book says this attack hits an "IKEv1-enabled device", but SA_INIT is an IKEv2 message, so it means an IKEv2 gateway.

lines.text: Lifetime: IKEv1 negotiates it in MM1 and MM2, and the responder's lifetime must be equal to or less than the initiator's, which caused vendor mismatches. IKEv2 lifetime is local and not negotiated; each peer rekeys or deletes when its own lifetime expires, and each peer can say who initiates the rekey.
lines.spoken: Lifetime: IKEv1 negotiates it in M.M. 1 and M.M. 2, and the responder's lifetime must be equal to or less than the initiator's, which caused vendor mismatches. IKEv2 lifetime is local and not negotiated; each peer rekeys or deletes when its own lifetime expires, and each peer can say who initiates the rekey.
